questions.question: If there is ice on your side mirror:

options.text: The roadway is probably icy too.
The roadway will not be icy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The roadway is probably icy too.
questions.explanation: If ice forms on your mirrors or wipers while driving, the road surface is likely icy as well.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to skip a step.
The form must be followed in order.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to skip a step.
questions.explanation: Following the same steps each time helps you remember them. A routine makes it less likely you will forget a step.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Only when the trailer is loaded
Only to test the trailer brakes
Only in bad weather when the trailer might skid

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: Near a railroad crossing:

options.text: You will hear every approaching train.
You may not hear a train, even if one is coming.
You will hear two short horn blasts if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train, even if one is coming.
questions.explanation: Never count on hearing a train horn. The operator may not sound it, or horns may be prohibited in that area. Even if the horn sounds, noise in your vehicle may prevent you from hearing it until the train is too close.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS):

options.text: Brake harder than you would without ABS.
Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way as you would without ABS.
Brake with less force than you would without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way as you would without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake a vehicle with ABS the same way you would brake a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights. High beam lights will reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When inspecting the exhaust system, which is NOT a concern?

options.text: Exhaust parts not touching fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust parts not touching fuel system parts
questions.explanation: Watch for loose or broken pipes, brackets, clamps, or bolts; exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other moving parts; and leaking exhaust parts. Parts that are not touching other systems are fine.

questions.question: If a train is approaching the railroad crossing:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Drive around any lowered crossing gates.
Stop and wait for the train to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: Never try to beat a train across the tracks. It is hard to judge a train's speed accurately. Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?

options.text: Keep the cab cool with the air conditioner or open window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the cab cool with the air conditioner or open window.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue, keep the cab cool using the air conditioner or opening a window. Avoid heavy foods and take rest breaks every two hours or 100 miles.

questions.question: When you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off right away.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and ABS should turn off immediately.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor
questions.explanation: Both brake systems share one air compressor. If the air compressor breaks, both systems will stop working.

questions.question: What should a safety belt do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Latch securely.
questions.explanation: When checking your vehicle, make sure the safety belt is mounted securely, adjusts properly, latches firmly, and has no tears or fraying.

questions.question: What are the rules for commercial vehicle drivers using cell phones?

options.text: They can use any cell phone while driving.
They can only use a hands-free phone while driving.
They can only use a cell phone on rural roads.
They can use a cell phone at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can only use a hands-free phone while driving.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicle drivers cannot use hand-held cell phones while driving. They may only use hands-free phones.

questions.question: How do you release a dolly's spring brakes before coupling?

options.text: Use the dolly parking brake control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the dolly parking brake control.
questions.explanation: Use the dolly parking brake control to release the spring brakes. This is the first step when positioning the dolly in front of the rear trailer.

questions.question: Where should air lines be securely connected?
questions.correctAnswerText: The proper glad hands.
questions.explanation: Air lines must be securely attached to the proper glad hands with no leaks. They should have enough slack to allow for easy turning.

questions.question: What equipment must truck tractors with air brakes have if built after March 1, 1997?
questions.correctAnswerText: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other air brake vehicles built on or after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Rely only on traffic control signals.
Never try to outdrive an approaching train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never try to outdrive an approaching train.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching a railroad crossing. You may not hear a train coming, and signals may not warn you. Never try to outdrive a train at a railroad crossing.

questions.question: How do you prevent a manual transmission vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch.
questions.explanation: To prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.

questions.question: How do fully-loaded rigs compare to empty rigs in terms of rollover risk?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over.
They are more likely to roll over.
They are just as likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity because of the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: When you turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. To avoid rolling over, drive slowly on entrance ramps, exit ramps, and curves. Avoid making quick lane changes when pulling trailers.
